blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Data strategy plays a central role in training large language models (LLMs). It governs the selection, weighting, and scheduling of training data, thereby determining the capabilities a model can acquire from a fixed data budget. We treat high-quality data as having high training-dependent utility, which depends on the target objective, the model, and its training state rather than on the text alone. Research in this area now spans pretraining and post-training, but related ideas use inconsistent terminology and evaluation protocols. This work reviews data strategies across the training lifecycle and formulates them as policies that allocate a training budget over candidate examples. We organise methods by their decision granularity, model dependence, and temporal adaptivity, then compare their computational requirements and empirical support. Fine-grained or state-dependent policies offer more control but incur additional scoring, search, or rollout costs. Evidence for transfer across model scales and comparable end-to-end cost remains limited. A continuously updated list of papers, along with their public implementations, is available at https://github.com/xuyj233/data_strategy_survey.
blocks.zh: 数据策略在培训大型语言模型(LLM)方面起核心作用. 它管理培训数据的选择、加权和时间安排,从而确定一个模型可从固定数据预算中获取的能力。 我们把高质量数据视为具有高度依赖培训的效用,这取决于目标目标、模式及其培训状态,而不是仅仅取决于文本。 这一领域的研究现在跨越培训前和培训后,但相关想法使用的术语和评价规程不一致。 这项工作审查整个培训周期的数据战略,并将这些战略制定为政策,将培训预算分配给候选实例。 我们通过决定颗粒性、模型依赖性和时间适应性来组织方法,然后比较它们的计算要求和经验支持。 精细或依赖国家的政策提供了更多的控制,但需要额外的评分、搜索或推出费用。 跨模型比额表和可比较的端到端费用转移的证据仍然有限。 在https://github.com/xuyj233/data_strategy_survey上可查到一份不断更新的论文清单及其公开执行。

blocks.en:
Training data is a major determinant of large language model (LLM)
performance ( Penedo et al., 2023 ; Penedo et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2024a ) .
Scaling laws quantify the effects of model size, compute, and token budget,
whereas data strategy determines which examples fill that
budget ( Kaplan et al., 2020 ; Hoffmann et al., 2022 ) . Data quality and
composition affect both downstream accuracy and training efficiency ( Xie et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2025b ; Ye et al., 2025 ) .

Across the LLM training lifecycle, data strategies 1 1 1 Including
selection, reweighting, and curricula. are shaped by the
distinct constraints of each phase. Pretraining
comprises stable training and annealing, with most work focusing on data
strategies during stable training. Owing to the scale of pretraining corpora,
methods in this phase typically optimise
mixtures at the domain level, commonly referred to as data mixing or
domain reweighting, by assigning one weight to each source or cluster ( Xie et al., 2023 ; Fan et al., 2024 ; Diao et al., 2025 ) .
Domain-level optimisation trades sample-level flexibility for tractability,
assuming the corpus admits a useful partition. During annealing, empirical approaches typically advocate
selecting high-quality data ( Dubey et al., 2024 ; Feng et al., 2024 ) . From a
theoretical perspective, Xu et al. (2026b) characterise annealing with a
river-valley model and argue that controlling updates along specific directions
guides the model towards a local minimum.

blocks.en:
Post-training data strategy is a multi-granularity control problem spanning
task-level mixing, data selection, and curriculum design. During supervised
fine-tuning, mixture-level methods balance transfer against interference and
forgetting across capabilities, while finer-grained methods select or order
instructions according to their relevance, influence, difficulty, or learning
progress ( Li et al., 2025a ; Wu et al., 2024 ; Xia et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2024b ; Liang et al., 2025a ) .
During preference optimisation, Corrado et al. (2025) prioritise tasks on which a generalist model lags behind task-specific
specialists. Related work on reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards
learns data mixtures that improve generalisation across heterogeneous
capabilities ( Liang et al., 2025b ) .

blocks.en:
Across these stages, the utility of training data depends on the target
capability, the base model, and its current training state. We therefore use high-quality in this training-dependent sense: an example is of high
quality for a training run when allocating budget to it improves the target
objective from the current model state. Rule-based filters and external
scorers approximate this utility with fixed, model-independent proxies,
whereas model-aware methods estimate it from losses, gradients, or curvature.
Section 2 makes this utility the objective of a data
policy.

blocks.en:
Data strategy is studied under separate names, including selection, pruning,
reweighting, mixture optimisation, and curricula, which obscures their shared
structure and complicates compute comparisons. Existing surveys cover
different parts of this landscape. Wang et al. (2023) study data management broadly across pretraining and
supervised fine-tuning, while Albalak et al. (2024) organise language-model
data selection around utility functions and selection mechanisms, with an
emphasis on pretraining. Other surveys focus specifically on instruction
tuning, categorising methods by selector type ( Zhang et al., 2025a ) or by quality, diversity, and importance ( Qin et al., 2025a ) ; Appendix Table 6 compares
their stage coverage. Our contributions are: • We cast selection, reweighting, mixing, and curricula as policy
optimisation over the training trajectory. • We review methods from pretraining to post-training, comparing
their assumptions, computational costs, and empirical evidence. • We compare partitions induced by three signals and reconstruct
auxiliary-training compute for representative data-mixture strategies.

Both stages instantiate Equation ( 1 ), while
differing in scale, supervision, pool dynamics, and model state. Standard
pretraining optimises next-token prediction over massive, largely static
corpora, favouring coarse domain-level decisions or infrequent rescoring.
Annealing and mid-training begin from an existing checkpoint but retain many
of the same scale constraints. Post-training uses instruction, preference, or
reward feedback. Its pool may be fixed for supervised fine-tuning and offline
preference optimisation, or evolve through model-generated rollouts in online
reinforcement learning. Smaller pools and richer feedback often make
fine-grained, model-conditioned policies more practical.

blocks.en:
Rule-based methods apply hand-crafted heuristics that require no learned model.
Table 1 groups them by the information a rule needs:
metadata such as the URL, statistics or patterns within a single document, or
comparisons across the corpus. Most open corpora, such as
RefinedWeb ( Penedo et al., 2023 ) and Dolma ( Soldaini et al., 2024 ) ,
combine the rules of C4 ( Raffel et al., 2020 ) and Gopher ( Rae et al., 2021 ) with exact or MinHash deduplication.
FineWeb ablates these rules one by one and replaces C4’s terminal-punctuation
rule, which removes about 30 % 30\% of tokens, with milder custom
filters ( Penedo et al., 2024 ) . Recent work makes the rules more adaptive:
FineWeb2 derives thresholds for each language from that language’s metric
distributions ( Penedo et al., 2025 ) , and prior-based filtering replaces
model perplexity with corpus-level token frequencies, cutting filtering time by
more than 1000 × 1000\times ( Seo et al., 2026 ) . Such rules are cheap and
transparent, but they capture only surface properties of a document rather than
its value for training, and their thresholds must be re-tuned for each corpus
or language.

information ( Minamoto et al., 2026 ) . QuaDMix combines

diversity ( Liu et al., 2025a ) .

that these scorers are independent of the model being trained, so the quality

Scorers are also sensitive to surface style. Rephrasing documents in Wikipedia

First-order methods score a document by its per-sample gradient,

direction ( Wang et al., 2026a ) . Grad-Mimic measures
how well a sample’s gradient aligns with a direction induced by a pretrained
reference model ( Huang et al., 2025 ) .

Second-order methods further account for curvature through the Hessian.
Pontryagin maximum principle-based data selection (PDS) casts selection as an

annealing ( Xu et al., 2026b ) . Dynamic directional graph-constrained data
scheduling (D 3 ) uses a second-order expansion to model asymmetric influence
between training units, then schedules data over the resulting directed
graph ( Xu et al., 2026a ) . Higher-order signals
capture interactions that lower-order ones miss, but are more expensive to
compute.

it is one cell in a partition 𝒫 = { 𝒟 k } k = 1 K \mathcal{P}=\{{\cal D}_{k}\}_{k=1}^{K} of the

Some studies partition a pretraining corpus using human-specified attributes,
most commonly data
source ( Xie et al., 2023 ; Fan et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2025b ; Li et al., 2025b ; Kang et al., 2025 ) or topic ( Peng et al., 2025 ; Zhu et al., 2025 ) .
These domains are easy to interpret and inspect, but they have two
limitations. First, a human-defined taxonomy may not align with the
distinctions that matter to the model. Corpora considered similar by humans
may induce different learning dynamics, whereas nominally different domains
may provide redundant training
signals ( Peng et al., 2025 ; Xu et al., 2026c ) . Second, some
corpora resist meaningful assignment
to a single domain. Web-derived corpora such as Pile-CC, for example, contain
heterogeneous topics, genres, and quality levels despite being treated as one
corpus-level domain. Topic-modelling methods can reduce reliance on manually
specified labels ( Peng et al., 2025 ; Zhu et al., 2025 ) ,
but the resulting partitions still depend on modelling assumptions and
assignment errors.

blocks.en:
More data selection methods now estimate the value of data relative to a
model and a target objective, using losses, gradients, or

The two signals fail differently. Distributional profiles depend on a
predefined taxonomy and can miss variation within a domain. Gradient scores
are local to a checkpoint and target set, so their ranking can change during
training. Recomputing them tracks that change but adds recurring cost.
Neither signal directly estimates marginal utility after full training. A
coverage gap identifies where a model is weak but not whether the available
examples will close that gap. Gradient alignment is more local and can assign
high scores to examples whose update directions are already represented.
Cached rankings therefore require validation after the checkpoint or target
distribution changes.

blocks.en: 4.2 Summary and Discussion
blocks.zh: 4.2 总结和讨论

blocks.en:
Post-training policies range from data-only Chameleon and checkpoint-based
LESS and ADG to stateful OASIS, EVIC, and
DynamixSFT ( Xie et al., 2025 ; Xia et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2026 ; Lee et al., 2026 ; Liang et al., 2025a ; Shin et al., 2025 ) .
Stateful policies can control inclusion, sampling frequency, and order; EDCO
spans all three ( Pang et al., 2026 ) . Outer
objectives now include worst-group loss and preservation of base-model
capabilities ( Corrado et al., 2025 ; Lu et al., 2025 ) .
Greater adaptivity makes scores more specific to the current model, but also
shortens how long they remain valid. Comparisons that ignore rescoring
frequency can conflate a better signal with additional model queries.

blocks.en:
Fixed-pool supervised fine-tuning leaves three further questions. For
environment and task selection, where should an agent interact during RL?
Unlike fixed-pool SFT, environments differ in rollout cost, reward reliability,
and skill coverage. WebRL filters tasks generated from prior failures by
feasibility and critic-estimated difficulty, but only within WebArena. How to
allocate a rollout budget across heterogeneous environments remains largely
unexplored ( Qi et al., 2025 ) . For selection efficiency, how can selection
remain cheaper than the rollouts it avoids? Curriculum RL with Off-Policy
Influence Guidance (CROPI) reuses initial-policy trajectories and compressed
gradients, yet recomputes features over a large candidate pool at each
phase ( Zhu et al., 2026 ) . Partial pools, learned proxies, and reusable
rollout buffers reduce this work but may become stale as the policy changes.
Finally, for granularity and credit assignment, what should be selected in a
long-horizon task? Selecting demonstration steps and pruning state context
improves offline web-agent training ( Zadeh et al., 2026 ) . Online RL jointly
chooses environments, tasks, trajectories, and transitions. Selection must
preserve trajectory coherence while attributing delayed terminal rewards to
intermediate decisions.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We cast selection, domain reweighting, and curricula as policies that allocate
a training budget over examples. Coarse decisions require a useful partition;
model awareness and adaptivity add scoring, proxy-training, or rollout cost.
Our analyses show that partitions depend on the construction signal and that
auxiliary floating-point operations (FLOPs) depend on model size, tokens per
run, and run count. Future evaluations should report utility and end-to-end
cost together, including for agentic RL policies.

blocks.en: Appendix A Related Surveys
blocks.zh: 附录A 相关调查

blocks.en:
Prior surveys establish broad taxonomies for selecting training data. Albalak et al. (2024) organise language-model data
selection around a utility function and the mechanism that converts utility
into inclusion or sampling decisions, covering pretraining, instruction
tuning, alignment, in-context learning, and task-specific adaptation. Wang et al. (2023) take a wider data-management
view encompassing quantity, quality, and domain/task composition, whereas Zhang et al. (2025a) focus specifically on
quality-oriented subset construction for instruction tuning. We treat
selection, domain reweighting, and curricula as restrictions on a common
time-varying weighting policy. This framing supports comparisons across
training stage, decision granularity, state dependence, and selection compute
(Table 6 ).

blocks.en:
Data-centric MLLM surveys broaden the candidate unit beyond text to aligned
image–text pairs, audio, video, and 3D data. Bai et al. (2024) follow the full multimodal data pipeline,
including collection, filtering and deduplication, pretraining selection and
modality mixing, adaptation, and dataset evaluation. Qin et al. (2025b) instead study data–model
co-development: multimodal data improve models, while models act as generators,
annotators, and evaluators of data. These surveys expose modality-specific
criteria such as cross-modal alignment and modality balance, but cover data
construction more broadly. We focus on the narrower optimisation question of
which existing training units to expose, at what weight, and at which training
state; under this formulation, multimodal methods change the utility signal and
group structure but share the same data policy abstraction.
blocks.zh:
数据中心 MLLM调查将候选单位从文本扩大到对齐
图像 - 文本对、 音频、 视频和 3D 数据 。 Bai等人(2024年)遵循完整的多式联运数据管道,
包括收集、过滤和复制、预训选择和
模式混合、适应和数据集评价。 秦等人(2025b)转而研究数据-模型
共同开发:多式联运数据改进模型,而模型则发挥发电机的作用,
注释员和数据评估员。 这些调查揭示了特定模式
标准,如跨模式协调和模式平衡,但涵盖数据
建设范围更广。 我们着重讨论较狭隘的优化问题:
* 现有培训单位应披露、数量和培训情况
状态;在此公式下,多式联运方法改变效用信号和
组结构但共享相同的数据政策抽象。

blocks.en: B.2 RQ1: How Do Different Partition Signals Define Domains?
blocks.zh: B.2 RQ1: 不同分区信号如何定义域?

blocks.en:
A domain is meaningful only relative to the signal used to construct it. We
therefore ask whether source metadata, semantic similarity, and model gradients
induce compatible partitions of the same documents.
blocks.zh:
一个域仅相对于用于构建它的信号来说是有意义的. 我们
因此询问源元数据、语义相似性和模型梯度是否
诱导同一文档的兼容分区。

blocks.en:
We sample 115,839 SlimPajama documents, with at most 20,000 from each of its
seven source categories ( Soboleva et al., 2023 ) . The source labels
provide the human-defined partition. For semantic-space domains, we encode
documents with stella_en_400M_v5 , 2 2 2 An English dense text-embedding model
released by NovaSearch for retrieval and semantic-similarity tasks. Here it
maps each document to a semantic vector for clustering. the encoder used by Nemotron-CLIMB ( Diao et al., 2025 ) . Gradient-space domains instead use projected,
L2-normalised gradients from Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, following the TRAK
construction ( Park et al., 2023 ) . We cluster the first 50 principal
components with KMeans using ten initialisations and seed 42. The main
comparison uses K = 7 K=7 , matching the number of source categories, and reports
normalised mutual information (NMI) and adjusted Rand index (ARI).

建筑(Park等人,2023年). 我们把前50名校长集中起来
含有KMEANs的组件,使用十种初始化和42种种子。 主体
比较使用 K = 7 K = 7, 匹配源类别的数目,以及报告
正常化的相互信息(NMI)和调整的兰德指数(ARI)。
